mapping_basis: The source manifest has ten numbered photos with their own caption labels #1 through #10, each mapping to the matching canonical stanza; there are no additional numbered photographs. #2, #7, #9 and #10 have substantial image-caption or canonical-scene mismatches; #1 is a split context collage; #3, #4, #5, #6 and #8 align thematically but still require canonical-first recomposition. The three nostanza images are non-scene Tamil text pages. No stanza has a photo gap, and no nostanza image is used.
source_photo_role: Facebook group pictures are attributed scene/context references only, not style or identity references, not approval.

references.caption:
#1
Long ago, Saubhari sage performed penance by submerging in the waters of Kaalindi, for twelve years, to have Bhagwan’s vision. He became attached to the fish who kept living there. Once he saw Garuda right in front of his eyes.
references.observed_reference: A split source collage places Saubhari meditating underwater beside a large Garuda taking a fish at the river surface.
references.mapping_note: The caption and stanza both center Saubhari’s underwater penance and sighting of Garuda; the collage compresses the two contexts. Recompose a coherent underwater view; do not copy its split layout.

references.caption:
#2
Garuda who was hungry ate a fish. Seeing that, Saubhari was very agitated and cursed Garuda saying that he would lose his life if he ate any creatures there.
references.observed_reference: A solitary sage meditates underwater; no Garuda, fish-taking action, or curse is visible.
references.mapping_note: Caption #2 is mapped by its own label, but the image omits the stanza’s decisive encounter and curse. Use only as Saubhari identity/context; canonical text controls the scene.

references.caption:
#3
At that time, Kaaliya the serpent was full of pride due to the power of his poison. He ate away the offerings kept for Garuda.. Angered at this, Garuda who is devoted to Bhagwan attacked Kaaliya and chased him. Knowing that Garuda will not come to the river Kaalindi due to sage Shoubari's curse, Kaaliya took refuge in it.
references.observed_reference: A large golden Garuda dives toward a many-hooded serpent in a river.
references.mapping_note: The image aligns with the pursuit of Kaliya by Garuda; canonical text supplies the prior theft of Garuda’s offering and Kaliya’s refuge in Kalindi.

references.caption:
#4
As the cruel Kaaliya was living in the waters of Kaalindi, the trees dried up and the birds who flew in the sky above, fell down dead. Bhagwan’s heart melted in compassion and was moved with pity seeing the plight of the creatures.
references.observed_reference: A simple cartoon scene shows a dead landscape, fallen tree, dark river, Krishna and cowherd boys.
references.mapping_note: The dead riverbank supports the poisoned-water setting and harm to life; the cartoon rendering and panel number are not style or scene instructions.

references.caption:
#5
On one hot summer day, Krishna went to the interior of the forest on the banks of the river Yamuna without his brother Balarama. The cows and cowherds which felt very thirsty drank the river water which was poisoned.
references.observed_reference: Krishna stands among thirsty cowherds and cattle by a dark river, with a serpent visible in the water.
references.mapping_note: The group’s drinking of poisoned Yamuna water on a hot day aligns with the canonical stanza; exclude unsupported staging and use the established Krishna contract.

references.caption:
#6
The cows and the Gopas soon fell dead on the ground. Krishna felt pity for the cows and Gopas and by His merciful glances, which were like showering nectar into their body, revived them back to life.
references.observed_reference: Krishna stands beside collapsed cowherds and cattle near a serpent in the wooded riverbank.
references.mapping_note: The fallen devotees and Krishna’s approach support stanza 6; depict the restorative sidelong glance without halo beams or rays.

references.caption:
#7
Gopas got up from ground wondering the feel of the bliss showered in their various parts of the body. They understood that is was Krishna’s divine act and hugged and thanked Krishna for saving them.
references.observed_reference: Krishna sits playing a flute under a tree among cowherd boys; cows graze behind them.
references.mapping_note: Caption #7 and stanza #7 describe the boys rising and embracing Krishna after recognizing his rescue; the photograph instead shows a flute scene. Treat as broad identity/context only.

references.caption:
#8
Like how the Gopas felt the flow of bliss in their bodies, even the cows felt grateful and surrounded Krishna with tears of joy.
references.observed_reference: Krishna stands in a forest stream surrounded by cows, calves, birds, and other animals.
references.mapping_note: The cows surrounding Krishna align broadly with stanza 8. Remove the watermark, unrelated wildlife, glossy rendering, and unsupported halo.

references.caption:
#9
Gopas had goosebumps all over their body. They were experiencing bliss which could not be expressed. Wondering if it was all due to the poison, the gopas fell at Krishna's feet and praised and prayed to him.
references.observed_reference: A pastoral scene shows Krishna seated with cows and boys nearby; there is no clear prostration or prayer.
references.mapping_note: Caption #9 maps to this image by its own #9 label, but the image omits the gopas’ wonder, horripilation, prostration, and praise. Use only pastoral context; follow Sanskrit.

references.caption:
#10
Thus Bhagwan revived his devotees by his merciful glances and rendered them devoid of any disease. Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan to protect him and release him of his disease with his merciful glances.
references.observed_reference: A crowded pastoral procession shows Krishna among many cows and cowherds, with a temple-side group.
references.mapping_note: Caption #10 describes the closing prayer for protection from illness; the image is a broad pastoral procession and does not depict Bhattathiri’s prayer or the stanza’s healing request. Use only contextual reference.
